definition: Child care refers to care provided in early learning and child care centres, where young children spend regular, repeated time in environments designed to support their development and play. In this context, child care includes the physical settings and features that shape how children behave and engage in activities such as outdoor play.

reasons: The packet does not define child care as care provided in early learning and child care centres; it only discusses those centres as settings for children’s outdoor play.

The claim that child care includes the physical settings and features that shape behavior is an inference from the article’s discussion of environmental play features and affordances, not a stated definition of the term.
The wording adds developmental/supportive and repeated-time details that are broader than the source support for this term.

The packet supports that early learning and child care centres support children’s regular, repeated, quality time in outdoor play, and that environmental play features are associated with children’s outdoor play behaviour; however, it does not explicitly support the claim that these centres/environments are “designed to support their development” (development is not stated in the provided text).

The packet focuses on outdoor play spaces and features (e.g., gardening areas, climbing structures, tricycle paths) and their association with play behaviour; it does not directly support the broader wording that physical settings/features “shape how children behave” in general beyond outdoor play engagement.
